questions.prompt: Overloaded methods must share the same:
questions.explanation: Overloads share a name but differ in parameters.

questions.prompt: Can two methods with the same name and parameters but different return types coexist?
options: No, this is a compile error
questions.explanation: Signature excludes return type, so this is not allowed.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank for an overload that accepts a double
questions.explanation: Using double differentiates this from an int overload.

questions.prompt: ref and out parameters affect overload resolution. Two methods differing only by ref vs out are:
questions.explanation: ref and out are part of the signature, so they can distinguish overloads.

questions.prompt: Implement Max(int a, int b) and Max(int a, int b, int c) returning the largest, then print Max(4,9,2)
Operator overloading lets you define behavior for:
options: Built-in operators like + on your types
questions.explanation: Operators such as + can be overloaded for custom types.

questions.prompt: Arrange these lines to create overloads differing by parameter order
questions.explanation: Swapping parameter order yields a valid overload.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank for an overload accepting a list of strings
questions.explanation: A different parameter type creates the overload.

questions.prompt: Which is true about overload resolution with optional parameters?
options: A call may match an overload with defaults
questions.explanation: Calls can bind to overloads that provide default values.

questions.prompt: Implement Concat(string a, string b) and Concat(string a, string b, string c) returning joined strings, then print Concat('a','b','c')
questions.explanation: The three-string overload should be used.
